note: Islamic Religious Studies round 3 (part A): the Qur'an, Hadith, Tawhid, attributes of Allah, faith, articles of faith, worship, Salah, Zakat, Sawm, Hajj, jihad and self-discipline - text-based and application items.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The Qur'an is divided into chapters and parts. The number of surahs (chapters) in the Qur'an is
questions.explanation: The Qur'an has 114 surahs; it is also divided into 30 parts (ajza') to ease recitation over a month.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: A student wants to recite the whole Qur'an in Ramadan, one part each night. He should follow the division of the Qur'an into
questions.A: sixty verses
questions.B: seven surahs
questions.C: thirty ajza' (juz')
questions.explanation: The 30 ajza' (singular juz') were marked so that the Qur'an can be completed in a month.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The first five verses revealed to the Prophet (SAW) in the cave of Hira belong to Surah
questions.A: An-Nasr (110)
questions.B: Al-Fatihah (1)
questions.C: Al-Muddaththir (74)
questions.explanation: Surah Al-Alaq opens with 'Iqra' (Read) and was the first revelation; Al-Muddaththir followed after a pause.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The longest surah in the Qur'an, which also contains the longest verse (the verse on debt), is
questions.A: Al-Kahf
questions.B: Al-Baqarah
questions.C: Yasin
questions.explanation: Al-Baqarah has 286 verses; its verse 282 on writing down debts is the longest single verse.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The only surah of the Qur'an that does not begin with 'Bismillahir-Rahmanir-Rahim' is
questions.A: An-Naml
questions.B: Al-Fatihah
questions.C: At-Tawbah
questions.explanation: At-Tawbah (9) has no Basmalah at its start; An-Naml (27) contains the Basmalah twice.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The Prophet (SAW) said that a certain surah is equal to one-third of the Qur'an because it summarises the doctrine of Tawhid. That surah is
questions.A: Al-Asr
questions.B: Al-Fatihah
questions.C: Al-Kawthar
questions.explanation: Surah Al-Ikhlas (112) declares the absolute oneness of Allah and is described as equal to a third of the Qur'an.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: A Muslim recites Surah Al-Falaq and Surah An-Nas every night before sleeping. These two surahs are together called
questions.A: as-Sab' al-Mathani (the seven oft-repeated)
questions.B: al-Mu'awwidhatayn (the two surahs of seeking refuge)
questions.C: al-Hawamim (the surahs beginning with Ha-Mim)
questions.explanation: Al-Falaq and An-Nas both begin 'Say: I seek refuge', hence al-Mu'awwidhatayn; az-Zahrawan are Al-Baqarah and Al Imran.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The verse known as Ayat al-Kursi (the Verse of the Throne), which the Prophet (SAW) described as the greatest verse in the Qur'an, is found in Surah
questions.A: Yasin (36:1)
questions.B: Al Imran (3:18)
questions.C: Al-Baqarah (2:255)
questions.explanation: Ayat al-Kursi is verse 255 of Surah Al-Baqarah and describes Allah's knowledge, power and sovereignty.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: 'This day I have perfected for you your religion, completed My favour upon you and chosen for you Islam as your religion' (5:3). This verse was revealed
questions.A: after the victory at the battle of Badr
questions.B: in the cave of Hira at the first revelation
questions.C: on the night of the Hijrah to Madinah
questions.D: at Arafat during the Farewell Pilgrimage in 10 AH
questions.explanation: The verse came down on the Day of Arafah during the Farewell Hajj, shortly before the Prophet's death.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: A verse says 'Rivalry in worldly increase distracts you until you visit the graves.' A Muslim who spends his life amassing wealth and boasting about it is warned by this verse of Surah
questions.A: Al-Ma'un
questions.B: At-Takathur
questions.C: Al-Fil
questions.explanation: Surah At-Takathur (102) condemns competition in piling up wealth and children until death arrives.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: Surah Al-Ma'un describes a person who repels the orphan, does not encourage feeding the poor, prays heedlessly to be seen and refuses small kindnesses. Such a person is described in the surah as one who
questions.A: fasts in the month of Ramadan
questions.B: has memorised the whole Qur'an
questions.C: denies the religion (the Judgement)
questions.D: gives Zakat on all his wealth
questions.explanation: The surah opens 'Have you seen the one who denies the Recompense?' and lists his conduct as evidence of that denial.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: Surah Al-Fil recounts how Allah destroyed the army of Abrahah that came with elephants to demolish the Ka'bah, by sending
questions.A: a violent earthquake in Makkah
questions.B: a great flood from the mountains
questions.C: an army of angels on horseback
questions.D: flocks of birds throwing stones of baked clay
questions.explanation: Surah 105 describes birds in flocks (ababil) pelting the army with stones of sijjil in the Year of the Elephant.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: 'With every hardship there is ease; indeed, with every hardship there is ease.' A student who has failed an examination and feels hopeless should draw comfort from these verses of Surah
questions.A: Al-Humazah
questions.B: Ash-Sharh (Al-Inshirah)
questions.C: Al-Lahab
questions.explanation: Surah 94 repeats the promise that ease accompanies hardship, and ends by directing the believer to turn to his Lord.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: In Surah Ad-Duha Allah reminds the Prophet (SAW) that He found him an orphan and gave him shelter. The surah therefore commands him
questions.A: to migrate at once from Makkah to Madinah with his family
questions.B: to fast for three days in every month of the year
questions.C: not to oppress the orphan nor repel the one who asks
questions.D: to build a mosque at Quba for the people of Madinah
questions.explanation: Surah 93 draws practical lessons from Allah's favours: do not oppress the orphan, do not drive away the beggar, and proclaim Allah's bounty.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: Surah Al-Kafirun ends with the words 'To you your religion and to me my religion.' It was revealed when the Quraysh proposed that
questions.A: a ten-year truce should be signed between the Muslims and Makkah
questions.B: the Muslims should leave Makkah and migrate across the sea to Abyssinia
questions.C: the Prophet (SAW) should become their king and share their wealth
questions.D: the Prophet (SAW) and they should take turns worshipping each other's gods
questions.explanation: The Quraysh offered a compromise of alternating worship; the surah rejected any mixing of Tawhid with idolatry.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: Surah Al-Humazah pronounces woe on every slanderer and backbiter who hoards wealth and counts it, thinking his wealth will make him immortal. His punishment is described as
questions.A: drowning in a great flood sent from the sky
questions.B: al-Hutamah, a fire that reaches the hearts
questions.C: being turned into stone on the spot
questions.D: expulsion from Makkah into the desert
questions.explanation: Surah 104 threatens the mocker and hoarder with al-Hutamah, the crushing fire of Allah.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: Surah Quraysh reminds the tribe of Quraysh of their safe winter and summer trade journeys and commands them to
questions.A: build a new house of worship at Ta'if and abandon the Ka'bah in Makkah for ever
questions.B: fight the tribes of Madinah who threatened their caravans on the roads to Syria and Yemen
questions.C: worship the Lord of this House who fed them against hunger and secured them against fear
questions.D: share the profits of their winter and summer journeys equally with the poor of Makkah
questions.explanation: Surah 106 links the Quraysh's security and prosperity to Allah, Lord of the Ka'bah, and calls them to worship Him alone.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: In Surah Luqman, the wise Luqman advises his son. Which of the following is among his counsels?
questions.A: 'Divide your inheritance equally between your sons and daughters'
questions.B: 'Migrate to Madinah when the persecution becomes severe'
questions.C: 'Perform the pilgrimage every year of your life'
questions.D: 'Do not associate anything with Allah; indeed, shirk is a great injustice'
questions.explanation: Luqman (31:13-19) warns against shirk, commands prayer and patience, and forbids arrogance and a loud voice.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: Surah Al-Hujurat (49:6) commands: 'O you who believe, if a wicked person brings you news, verify it.' A Muslim who forwards a WhatsApp rumour without checking has ignored this command against
questions.A: wearing gold and silk
questions.B: spreading unverified information
questions.C: eating without saying Bismillah
questions.explanation: The verse requires believers to investigate reports before acting on them, lest they harm people in ignorance.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: Makkan surahs differ from Madinan surahs in that Makkan surahs generally
questions.A: address the hypocrites and the People of the Book in Madinah
questions.B: are long and contain detailed laws on inheritance, marriage and warfare
questions.C: are short, emphasise Tawhid, the Hereafter and stories of earlier prophets
questions.D: were revealed after the Hijrah and begin with 'O you who believe'
questions.explanation: Makkan revelation built faith; Madinan revelation (after the Hijrah) legislated for the new community.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The Qur'an was revealed in Arabic and has been preserved unchanged. The Qur'an itself attributes this preservation to
questions.A: the monks of Abyssinia, who copied it into their language for the Negus
questions.B: the Quraysh, who kept the written copies in the Ka'bah under armed guard
questions.C: the Byzantine emperor Heraclius, who ordered copies to be made for his library
questions.D: Allah, who says 'It is We who sent down the Reminder and We will guard it' (15:9)
questions.explanation: Surah Al-Hijr 15:9 states that Allah Himself guards the Qur'an from corruption.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The scribe who compiled the Qur'an into one volume under Abu Bakr and later headed Uthman's committee for the standard copy was
questions.A: Bilal ibn Rabah
questions.B: Zayd ibn Thabit
questions.C: Khalid ibn al-Walid
questions.explanation: Zayd ibn Thabit, the Prophet's chief scribe, collected the Qur'an from written pieces and memorisers.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: Tajwid is important in the study of the Qur'an because it
questions.A: translates the Qur'an into local languages for non-Arabs
questions.B: explains the historical occasions on which verses were revealed
questions.C: ensures that each letter is pronounced correctly from its point of articulation
questions.D: arranges the surahs in the order of their revelation
questions.explanation: Tajwid is the science of correct recitation; asbab an-nuzul deals with occasions of revelation.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: A verse states: 'We have certainly created man in the best of stature' (95:4). This verse is from Surah
questions.A: Al-Adiyat
questions.B: Al-Qadr
questions.C: Al-Bayyinah
questions.explanation: Surah At-Tin swears by the fig and the olive and declares man's noble creation, then warns of his fall through disbelief.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: Surah Al-Qari'ah describes the Day of Judgement, when people will be like scattered moths and mountains like carded wool. A person whose scales are light will have as his abode
questions.A: a garden beneath which rivers flow
questions.B: Hawiyah, a blazing fire
questions.C: the plain of Arafat
questions.explanation: Surah 101 says the one whose deeds weigh light will have 'a mother' (abode) of Hawiyah, which is a raging fire.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The term 'wahy' in Islamic teaching means
questions.A: the pilgrimage to Makkah in Dhul-Hijjah
questions.B: the call to prayer made by the mu'adhdhin
questions.C: divine revelation sent by Allah to His prophets
questions.D: the annual charity paid before Eid
questions.explanation: Wahy is Allah's communication to His messengers, mainly through the angel Jibril.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: A Hadith consists of two parts: the chain of narrators and the actual text. These are called respectively
questions.A: surah and ayah
questions.B: matn and sanad
questions.C: sahih and da'if
questions.explanation: The sanad is the chain of transmitters; the matn is the wording of the report.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: In Islamic terminology, Hadith refers to
questions.A: the verses revealed in Makkah only
questions.B: the sayings, actions and tacit approvals of the Prophet (SAW)
questions.C: the rulings of the four rightly guided caliphs
questions.explanation: Hadith (and Sunnah) record what the Prophet said, did or silently approved.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: A Hadith reported by so many narrators in every generation that they could not possibly have agreed on a lie is classified as
questions.A: da'if
questions.B: ahad
questions.C: mutawatir
questions.explanation: Mutawatir Hadith are established by overwhelming transmission; ahad Hadith have fewer narrators.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: A report whose chain contains a narrator known to be a liar and whose text contradicts the Qur'an is classified as
questions.A: mutawatir (mass-transmitted)
questions.B: sahih (sound)
questions.C: hasan (good)
questions.explanation: Fabricated Hadith are rejected entirely; the Prophet warned that whoever lies about him takes his seat in the Fire.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: A Hadith whose chain is unbroken but one of whose narrators has slightly weaker memory than is required for sahih is classified as
questions.A: mawdu'
questions.B: hasan
questions.C: munkar
questions.explanation: Hasan Hadith fall just below sahih in the reliability of a narrator's memory but are accepted as evidence.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The two most authentic collections of Hadith, known together as the Sahihayn, were compiled by
questions.A: an-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah
questions.B: Abu Dawud and at-Tirmidhi
questions.C: Imam al-Bukhari and Imam Muslim
questions.explanation: Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim are the most authoritative books after the Qur'an.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The Kutub as-Sittah (six canonical books of Hadith) are Bukhari, Muslim, Abu Dawud, at-Tirmidhi, an-Nasa'i and
questions.A: Sunan ad-Darimi
questions.B: al-Muwatta of Malik
questions.C: Musnad Ahmad
questions.explanation: Sunan Ibn Majah completes the six books; Malik's Muwatta is earlier but not counted among the six.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: A Hadith in which the Prophet (SAW) relates words whose meaning is from Allah but whose wording is the Prophet's own, and which is not part of the Qur'an, is called
questions.A: Hadith Mawquf
questions.B: Hadith Qudsi
questions.C: Hadith Maqtu'
questions.explanation: Hadith Qudsi ('sacred Hadith') convey Allah's words through the Prophet, e.g. 'O My servants, I have forbidden oppression for Myself.'

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The Prophet (SAW) said: 'Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day should speak good or remain silent.' A student who is about to insult a classmate but stops himself is applying this Hadith by
questions.A: giving sadaqah
questions.B: fasting on Monday
questions.C: guarding his tongue
questions.explanation: The Hadith links faith to controlling speech; harmful talk should be replaced by silence.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: A man came to the Prophet (SAW) and asked for advice. The Prophet said, 'Do not become angry,' and repeated it several times. The lesson is that
questions.A: advice should be sought only from elderly people
questions.B: anger is permitted as long as nobody is injured
questions.C: a Muslim should never give advice more than once
questions.D: controlling anger is a mark of strong faith and prevents many sins
questions.explanation: Anger leads to quarrels, injustice and broken ties; suppressing it is repeatedly praised in the Sunnah.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The Prophet (SAW) said: 'The halal is clear and the haram is clear, and between them are doubtful matters.' He advised that a Muslim who avoids doubtful matters
questions.A: must give away all his wealth to the poor and live only on what people give him
questions.B: protects his religion and his honour, like a shepherd who keeps away from a private pasture
questions.C: is excused from the five daily prayers until he is certain that his food is halal
questions.D: may eat whatever he likes on a journey since the doubt is removed by travelling
questions.explanation: The Hadith compares doubtful matters to the edge of a forbidden pasture; keeping clear of them keeps one from falling into haram.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The Prophet (SAW) said: 'Whoever among you sees an evil should change it with his hand; if he cannot, then with his tongue; if he cannot, then with his heart, and that is the weakest of faith.' A student who sees classmates cheating and quietly reports it to the invigilator has changed the evil with his
questions.A: heart
questions.B: hand
questions.C: tongue
questions.explanation: Speaking out or reporting is changing evil with the tongue; physically stopping it is with the hand; disapproving silently is with the heart.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The Prophet (SAW) said: 'The believers in their mutual love, mercy and compassion are like one body: when one limb aches, the whole body responds with sleeplessness and fever.' This Hadith teaches
questions.A: the rites of Hajj
questions.B: the rules of ablution
questions.C: the method of slaughtering animals
questions.explanation: The Hadith uses the image of a single body to describe the unity and mutual care of the ummah.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: According to a Hadith, the signs of a hypocrite are three: when he speaks he lies, when he promises he breaks it, and when he is trusted he
questions.A: gives more than required
questions.B: betrays the trust
questions.C: prays at night
questions.explanation: The Hadith in Bukhari and Muslim lists lying, breaking promises and betraying trusts as marks of hypocrisy.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The Prophet (SAW) said: 'Cleanliness (purity) is half of faith.' A Muslim who keeps his body, clothes and surroundings clean is
questions.A: excused from performing ablution before prayer
questions.B: performing an act that has no religious value
questions.C: fulfilling an important part of his religion
questions.explanation: Physical and spiritual purity are integral to Islam; taharah precedes worship.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The Prophet (SAW) said: 'Allah does not look at your bodies or your appearance, but He looks at your hearts and your deeds.' This Hadith teaches that
questions.A: physical beauty guarantees Paradise
questions.B: Muslims should not care about cleanliness
questions.C: wealthy people are closer to Allah
questions.D: sincerity and conduct matter more than outward looks
questions.explanation: Allah judges by inner sincerity and actions, not by physical features or status.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The Prophet (SAW) said: 'The most beloved deeds to Allah are those done regularly, even if they are small.' A Muslim who reads one page of the Qur'an every day rather than a whole juz' once a month is following this Hadith by
questions.A: avoiding the Qur'an on weekdays
questions.B: being consistent in worship
questions.C: reading only in Ramadan
questions.explanation: Steadiness in good deeds is preferred to occasional bursts of effort.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The Prophet (SAW) said: 'He who does not show mercy to people, Allah will not show mercy to him.' This Hadith encourages
questions.A: strictness in collecting debts
questions.B: harshness in correcting children
questions.C: compassion towards all creatures
questions.explanation: Mercy to others is a condition for receiving Allah's mercy.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The Prophet (SAW) said: 'Take advantage of five before five: your youth before old age, your health before sickness, your wealth before poverty, your free time before you become busy, and your life before your death.' The Hadith teaches Muslims to
questions.A: spend all their wealth immediately
questions.B: wait until old age to become religious
questions.C: avoid working while young
questions.D: use their opportunities before they are lost
questions.explanation: The Hadith urges prompt use of blessings that will not last.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The Prophet (SAW) said: 'Every one of you is a shepherd and is responsible for his flock.' According to the Hadith, a woman in her husband's house is a shepherd over
questions.A: the affairs of the state
questions.B: his household and children
questions.C: the mosque and its imam
questions.explanation: The Hadith names the ruler over his people, the man over his family, the woman over her husband's house and children, and the servant over his master's property.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The Prophet (SAW) said: 'Richness is not having many possessions; richness is the richness of the soul (contentment).' A poor labourer who is grateful and content while a millionaire is anxious for more illustrates that
questions.A: labourers should not seek higher pay
questions.B: money always brings happiness
questions.C: true wealth is contentment of the heart
questions.D: gratitude is required only from the rich
questions.explanation: Contentment (qana'ah) makes a person truly rich regardless of possessions.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: A Hadith attributed to a companion's own statement, not raised to the Prophet (SAW), is classified as
questions.A: mutawatir
questions.B: marfu'
questions.C: qudsi
questions.explanation: Marfu' reports go back to the Prophet; mawquf stop at a companion; maqtu' stop at a successor (tabi'i).

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.topic: Tawhid and the Oneness of Allah
questions.q: Tawhid means
questions.A: belief in the six articles of faith
questions.B: belief in the absolute oneness of Allah
questions.C: the five daily prayers
questions.explanation: Tawhid is the foundation of Islam: Allah is One in His lordship, worship and attributes.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.topic: Tawhid and the Oneness of Allah
questions.q: A man believes that Allah alone created the universe, but he prays to a dead saint at his grave to grant him children. He has violated
questions.A: the rules of ablution
questions.B: Tawhid ar-Rububiyyah (oneness of lordship)
questions.C: Tawhid al-Uluhiyyah (oneness of worship)
questions.explanation: Directing worship or supplication to other than Allah breaks Tawhid al-Uluhiyyah even if one accepts Allah as Creator.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.topic: Tawhid and the Oneness of Allah
questions.q: Tawhid ar-Rububiyyah is the belief that
questions.A: angels record human deeds
questions.B: prayer should be performed five times daily
questions.C: the Prophet (SAW) is the last messenger
questions.D: Allah alone creates, sustains and controls the universe
questions.explanation: Rububiyyah concerns Allah's lordship over creation; Uluhiyyah concerns worship; Asma wa Sifat concerns His names and attributes.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.topic: Tawhid and the Oneness of Allah
questions.q: The opposite of Tawhid, which the Qur'an calls the one sin Allah will not forgive if a person dies upon it, is
questions.A: riba (taking or giving usury)
questions.B: shirk (associating partners with Allah)
questions.C: ghibah (backbiting a Muslim)
questions.explanation: Qur'an 4:48: 'Allah does not forgive that partners be associated with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills.'

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.topic: Tawhid and the Oneness of Allah
questions.q: The Prophet (SAW) said: 'The thing I fear most for you is minor shirk,' and explained it as
questions.A: missing Fajr prayer
questions.B: eating pork
questions.C: riya' (showing off in worship)
questions.explanation: Riya' - performing good deeds to be seen by people - is called minor shirk because it directs part of the intention away from Allah.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.topic: Tawhid and the Oneness of Allah
questions.q: A student gives a large donation at the mosque mainly so that people will call him generous. His act is spoilt by
questions.A: nifaq al-akbar, major hypocrisy
questions.B: bid'ah, an innovation
questions.C: kufr, disbelief
questions.D: riya', a form of minor shirk
questions.explanation: Deeds done for human praise rather than for Allah are tainted by riya'.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.topic: Tawhid and the Oneness of Allah
questions.q: Surah Al-Ikhlas declares that Allah 'begets not, nor was He begotten, and there is none comparable to Him.' This refutes the belief that
questions.A: Allah created the heavens
questions.B: Allah has a son or a partner
questions.C: angels obey Allah
questions.explanation: The surah denies offspring, parentage and any equal to Allah.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.topic: Tawhid and the Oneness of Allah
questions.q: Belief that a particular stone, tree or river can bring fortune or misfortune independently of Allah is
questions.A: permitted, because the objects are part of creation
questions.B: sunnah, because the Prophet honoured the Black Stone
questions.C: shirk, because power over benefit and harm belongs to Allah alone
questions.D: wajib, because it strengthens faith in nature
questions.explanation: Attributing independent power to created things is associating partners with Allah.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.topic: Tawhid and the Oneness of Allah
questions.q: The Kalimat ash-Shahadah has two parts. The second part, 'Muhammadur Rasulullah', requires a Muslim to
questions.A: learn the Arabic language
questions.B: worship the Prophet (SAW) alongside Allah
questions.C: perform Hajj every year
questions.D: obey the Prophet (SAW) and follow his Sunnah
questions.explanation: Testifying that Muhammad is Allah's Messenger means accepting his teaching and obeying his commands, not worshipping him.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.topic: Tawhid and the Oneness of Allah
questions.q: A Muslim who says 'If Allah wills and you will' is corrected by the Prophet (SAW) to say 'If Allah alone wills.' The correction protects
questions.A: the grammar of the Arabic sentence and the order of its words
questions.B: Tawhid, by not placing a creature alongside Allah in the will
questions.C: the rules of the Friday sermon delivered by the imam
questions.D: the etiquette of eating with the right hand
questions.explanation: Even in speech a Muslim avoids expressions that equate created beings with Allah.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.topic: Tawhid and the Oneness of Allah
questions.q: Tawhid influences a Muslim's daily life by
questions.A: allowing him to break promises made to non-Muslims without any sin
questions.B: excusing him from work and effort since Allah provides everything
questions.C: making him fear and depend on Allah alone rather than on people or charms
questions.D: requiring him to live in isolation far away from other people
questions.explanation: A believer in Tawhid trusts Allah, is not enslaved by fear of creatures, and works honestly relying on Him.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.topic: Tawhid and the Oneness of Allah
questions.q: The Qur'an argues for Tawhid by saying: 'Had there been in the heavens and the earth gods besides Allah, both would have been ruined' (21:22). The argument is that
questions.A: the earth will one day be destroyed
questions.B: there are many gods who cooperate
questions.C: the heavens were created before the earth
questions.D: the orderly universe shows that it has one controller
questions.explanation: Multiple independent controllers would produce conflict and chaos; the harmony of creation points to one God.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.topic: Tawhid and the Oneness of Allah
questions.q: Kufr (disbelief) differs from shirk in that kufr is
questions.A: worship of idols, whereas shirk is denial of the Hereafter
questions.B: rejection of Allah or His message, whereas shirk is associating partners with Him
questions.C: a minor sin, whereas shirk is forgiven easily
questions.D: the same as riya', whereas shirk is the same as nifaq
questions.explanation: A kafir rejects faith outright; a mushrik may acknowledge Allah but gives others a share in what is His alone.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.topic: Tawhid and the Oneness of Allah
questions.q: The word 'Islam' means
questions.A: the five pillars
questions.B: the land of the Arabs
questions.C: submission to the will of Allah
questions.explanation: Islam is peace attained through submission to Allah alone.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.topic: Tawhid and the Oneness of Allah
questions.q: A Muslim doctor treats a patient and says, 'I have done my best; the cure is from Allah.' This statement reflects
questions.A: kufr, since he doubts his own skill
questions.B: shirk, since medicine should not be used
questions.C: riya', since he mentions his effort
questions.D: correct Tawhid, since healing ultimately belongs to Allah
questions.explanation: Taking means is required, while believing that results come from Allah alone.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The Prophet (SAW) said that Allah has ninety-nine names, and whoever memorises (and lives by) them will enter Paradise. These names are called
questions.A: al-Kutub as-Sittah
questions.B: al-Asma al-Husna
questions.C: al-Khulafa ar-Rashidun
questions.explanation: Al-Asma al-Husna (7:180) are the names of Allah found in the Qur'an and Sunnah.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The name Al-Khaliq means
questions.A: the Forgiving
questions.B: the Provider
questions.C: the Creator
questions.explanation: Al-Khaliq: Allah brings everything into existence from nothing.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: A Muslim who has sinned greatly repents sincerely, trusting that Allah accepts repentance. He is relying on Allah's names
questions.A: Al-Awwal and Al-Akhir
questions.B: Al-Jabbar and Al-Qahhar
questions.C: Al-Muhyi and Al-Mumit
questions.explanation: At-Tawwab (Acceptor of repentance) and Al-Ghafur (Oft-Forgiving) describe Allah's mercy to those who repent.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: A Muslim tempted to cheat when no one is watching remembers that Allah is As-Sami' and Al-Basir. These names mean that Allah is
questions.A: the Creator and the Provider
questions.B: the All-Hearing and the All-Seeing
questions.C: the First and the Last
questions.explanation: Awareness that Allah hears and sees everything restrains a believer even in secret.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The names Al-Adl and Al-Hakam describe Allah as
questions.A: the Guide and the Light
questions.B: the Living and the Self-Subsisting
questions.C: the Just and the Judge
questions.explanation: Al-Adl (the Utterly Just) and Al-Hakam (the Judge) assure believers that no injustice will remain unaddressed.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: Ayat al-Kursi describes Allah as Al-Hayy and Al-Qayyum, meaning
questions.A: the Opener of doors and the All-Knowing
questions.B: the Most Gracious and the Most Merciful
questions.C: the Sovereign King and the Most Holy
questions.explanation: Al-Hayy has perfect life without death; Al-Qayyum needs nothing and sustains everything.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The attributes of Allah are unlike those of created beings. The Qur'an states this principle in the verse
questions.A: 'And We have certainly honoured the children of Adam' (17:70)
questions.B: 'There is nothing like unto Him, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing' (42:11)
questions.C: 'Fasting is prescribed for you as it was prescribed for those before you' (2:183)
questions.explanation: Surah Ash-Shura 42:11 affirms Allah's attributes while denying any resemblance to creation.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: A poor widow prays for provision and soon finds work. The name of Allah most directly reflected in this experience is
questions.A: Al-Muntaqim (the Avenger)
questions.B: Al-Mumit (the Giver of Death)
questions.C: Ar-Razzaq (the Provider)
questions.explanation: Ar-Razzaq provides sustenance for all creatures.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The names Ar-Rahman and Ar-Rahim, which begin every surah except one, mean
questions.A: the Living and the Eternal
questions.B: the Just and the Wise
questions.C: the Mighty and the Compeller
questions.D: the Most Gracious and the Most Merciful
questions.explanation: Both derive from rahmah (mercy): Ar-Rahman is boundless mercy to all; Ar-Rahim is special mercy to believers.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The attribute of Allah that means He knows everything, including secret thoughts and future events, is
questions.A: Al-Wahhab (the Bestower)
questions.B: Al-Alim (the All-Knowing)
questions.C: Al-Karim (the Generous)
questions.explanation: Allah's knowledge encompasses all things, open and hidden, past and future.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: Muslims believe Allah's attributes are eternal. This means that
questions.A: the attributes were given to Allah by the angels
questions.B: Allah acquired knowledge after creating the universe
questions.C: Allah was always the Creator, the Knower and the Powerful, without beginning
questions.D: the attributes change from one age to another
questions.explanation: Allah's attributes are not acquired or lost; they belong to His eternal essence.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: As-Samad, used in Surah Al-Ikhlas, describes Allah as
questions.A: the Angel who brings down revelation
questions.B: the One who gives life to the dead
questions.C: the Guardian of the gates of Paradise
questions.D: the Eternal Refuge on whom all depend
questions.explanation: As-Samad is the Self-Sufficient Master to whom all creatures turn in need.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: A Muslim ruler who remembers that Allah is Al-Malik (the Sovereign) and Malik al-Mulk (Owner of all dominion) should
questions.A: consider himself above the law since he holds the highest office
questions.B: rule humbly, knowing that his authority is a trust from the true King
questions.C: demand worship from his subjects as the representative of Allah
questions.D: keep the treasury for his family since the kingdom belongs to him
questions.explanation: All power belongs to Allah; human authority is temporary and accountable.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: In the Hadith of Jibril, the angel asked the Prophet (SAW) about Islam, Iman and Ihsan. Iman was defined as belief in
questions.A: worshipping Allah as though you see Him, knowing that He sees you
questions.B: the Shahadah, Salah, Zakat, Sawm in Ramadan and Hajj to the House
questions.C: Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers, the Last Day and divine decree
questions.D: the Qur'an and the authentic Hadith of the Prophet only
questions.explanation: The six articles of faith define Iman; the five pillars define Islam; Ihsan is excellence in worship.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: A Muslim performs all the outward rituals but harbours no belief in his heart. According to Islamic teaching he has
questions.A: committed shirk by praying
questions.B: perfect Iman because actions are all that count
questions.C: reached the level of Ihsan
questions.D: Islam in form but lacks Iman, which is belief in the heart
questions.explanation: Iman is conviction in the heart, confession by the tongue and action by the limbs; outward acts alone are hypocrisy if belief is absent.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The Prophet (SAW) said: 'Faith has seventy-odd branches; the highest is saying La ilaha illa Allah and the lowest is removing a harmful thing from the road.' This teaches that
questions.A: faith is limited to the declaration of Tawhid
questions.B: faith covers belief, worship and everyday good conduct
questions.C: road maintenance is one of the five pillars
questions.explanation: Iman is comprehensive, ranging from creed to small acts of public benefit.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: According to the Qur'an, true believers are those whose hearts tremble when Allah is mentioned and whose faith increases when
questions.A: they win an argument
questions.B: they acquire more wealth
questions.C: His verses are recited to them
questions.explanation: Surah Al-Anfal 8:2 describes the believers whose faith grows with the Qur'an and who rely on their Lord.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: A Muslim who is going through severe hardship says, 'Allah tests those He loves,' and remains patient. This shows that Iman
questions.A: requires complaining to people
questions.B: removes all difficulties from life
questions.C: is proven only by wealth and success
questions.D: gives strength and hope in adversity
questions.explanation: Faith provides meaning in trials and the assurance of Allah's reward for patience.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The Prophet (SAW) said: 'None of you truly believes until he loves for his brother what he loves for himself.' A trader who sells his customers the same quality he would buy for his own family is
questions.A: showing off his goods to attract more customers
questions.B: demonstrating complete faith through fair dealing
questions.C: practising a form of minor shirk in his business
questions.D: breaking the rules that govern the payment of Zakat
questions.explanation: Faith is expressed in wishing others the good one wishes for oneself.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: Ihsan, the highest level of religion, was defined by the Prophet (SAW) as worshipping Allah
questions.A: with the largest possible congregation gathered behind one imam
questions.B: only inside the mosque on Fridays and on the two days of Eid
questions.C: as though you see Him, and if you do not see Him, knowing that He sees you
questions.D: in the Arabic language only, without any translation into other tongues
questions.explanation: Ihsan is excellence and sincerity born of constant awareness of Allah.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: Taqwa, which the Qur'an calls the best provision, means
questions.A: the ability to memorise a large number of Hadith with their chains
questions.B: wealth saved for the journey of Hajj and the sacrifice at Mina
questions.C: knowledge of Arabic grammar needed to understand the Qur'an
questions.D: consciousness of Allah that leads one to obey Him and avoid sin
questions.explanation: Taqwa (God-consciousness) is the inner guard against disobedience; 'the noblest of you is the most God-conscious' (49:13).

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The Qur'an says 'The believers are but brothers' (49:10). The social significance of faith shown here is that Iman
questions.A: restricts friendship to one's own tribe
questions.B: creates a bond of brotherhood beyond tribe, race and nationality
questions.C: requires every believer to be related by blood
questions.explanation: Shared faith unites Muslims of different backgrounds into one ummah.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: A Muslim believes that Allah sees him at all times and therefore does not steal even when he could escape detection. This effect of faith on conduct is known as
questions.A: qasr (shortening prayer)
questions.B: tayammum (dry ablution)
questions.C: muraqabah (awareness of Allah's watchfulness)
questions.explanation: Muraqabah, the sense of being watched by Allah, is the practical fruit of Iman and Ihsan.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The Prophet (SAW) said that a believer who commits adultery or theft is not a believer at the moment he does it. Scholars explain this as meaning that
questions.A: such a person must repeat the Shahadah before witnesses to re-enter Islam
questions.B: he becomes a disbeliever permanently and can never return to the fold of Islam
questions.C: faith and sin can never exist in one person at the same moment in any way
questions.D: his faith is diminished and its light withdrawn while he sins, not that he leaves Islam
questions.explanation: Iman increases with obedience and decreases with sin; major sins weaken faith without necessarily nullifying it.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: Which of the following best shows that Iman must be accompanied by action?
questions.A: The Qur'an mentions the number of angels in Paradise
questions.B: The Qur'an repeatedly says 'those who believe and do righteous deeds'
questions.C: The Qur'an describes the trade journeys of Quraysh
questions.D: The Qur'an forbids the eating of pork
questions.explanation: Belief and righteous action are paired dozens of times in the Qur'an (e.g. Surah Al-Asr).

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: A Muslim who says 'I believe in Allah' and then remains steadfast in obedience despite pressure is following the Prophet's advice to Sufyan ibn Abdullah:
questions.A: 'Fast three days in every month of the year'
questions.B: 'Migrate to Abyssinia and stay there'
questions.C: 'Say: I believe in Allah, and then be steadfast'
questions.D: 'Pray the night prayer and never leave it'
questions.explanation: The Hadith summarises religion as faith followed by steadfastness (istiqamah).

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The significance of faith for society is best illustrated by
questions.A: a community that prays five times a day in congregation but neglects its orphans and widows
questions.B: a community that has built many beautiful mosques but in which fraud and cheating are widespread
questions.C: a community that fasts the whole of Ramadan every year but oppresses its workers and servants
questions.D: a community in which people keep trusts, tell the truth and help the weak because they fear Allah
questions.explanation: Genuine Iman produces trustworthiness, justice and compassion in social life.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The number of articles of faith (arkan al-Iman) in Islam is
questions.A: five
questions.B: six
questions.C: seven
questions.explanation: Belief in Allah, angels, books, messengers, the Last Day and divine decree (qadar).

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The angel who will blow the trumpet to announce the Day of Resurrection is
questions.A: Mika'il
questions.B: Jibril
questions.C: Israfil
questions.explanation: Israfil blows the Sur; Jibril brings revelation; Mika'il is charged with rain and provision; Malik guards Hell.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The two angels who question a person in the grave about his Lord, his religion and his prophet are
questions.A: Jibril and Mika'il
questions.B: Raqib and Atid
questions.C: Harut and Marut
questions.explanation: Munkar and Nakir question the dead; Raqib and Atid record deeds on the right and left.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: A Muslim remembers that every word he utters is recorded, as the Qur'an says 'Not a word does he utter but there is a watcher ready' (50:18). The angels responsible are
questions.A: Munkar and Nakir
questions.B: Raqib and Atid
questions.C: Israfil and Izra'il
questions.explanation: The noble scribes record good deeds on the right and bad deeds on the left.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: Angels are described in Islam as beings created from
questions.A: smokeless fire, who can be good or evil
questions.B: clay, who have free will
questions.C: light, who never disobey Allah
questions.D: water, who live in the seas
questions.explanation: Angels are created from light and always obey; jinn are from smokeless fire; man from clay.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The Prophet (SAW) is called Khatam an-Nabiyyin (33:40). A man in Nigeria who claims to be a new prophet after Muhammad (SAW) contradicts the article of faith concerning
questions.A: divine decree, since prophethood is inherited
questions.B: the angels, since only angels bring revelation
questions.C: the Last Day, since prophets appear only at the end
questions.D: the messengers, since Muhammad is the last prophet
questions.explanation: Belief in the finality of Muhammad's prophethood is part of belief in the messengers.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The five messengers of strong will (Ulul-Azm) mentioned in the Qur'an are
questions.A: Adam, Idris, Hud, Salih and Lut
questions.B: Nuh, Ibrahim, Musa, Isa and Muhammad
questions.C: Dawud, Sulayman, Yunus, Zakariyya and Yahya
questions.D: Isma'il, Ishaq, Ya'qub, Yusuf and Ayyub
questions.explanation: Surah Al-Ahzab 33:7 and Ash-Shura 42:13 name these five as the greatest messengers.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The difference between a nabi and a rasul is that a rasul
questions.A: lived only in Arabia, while a nabi lived elsewhere
questions.B: is an angel, while a nabi is a human being
questions.C: is sent with a new law or scripture to a people, while a nabi follows an existing law
questions.D: is mentioned in the Hadith only, while a nabi is in the Qur'an
questions.explanation: Every rasul is a nabi, but not every nabi is a rasul; a rasul brings a new message.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The number of prophets mentioned by name in the Qur'an is
questions.A: ninety-nine
questions.B: one hundred and fourteen
questions.C: twelve
questions.explanation: Twenty-five prophets are named, from Adam to Muhammad (SAW); many others were sent whose names are not given.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: Belief in the Last Day includes belief in the Mizan. The Mizan is
questions.A: the bridge stretched over the Fire
questions.B: the scale on which deeds will be weighed
questions.C: the pool of the Prophet on the Last Day
questions.D: the trumpet that Israfil will blow
questions.explanation: Deeds are weighed on the Mizan; the Sirat is the bridge; the Hawd is the Prophet's pool.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: A farmer plants his crops carefully, prays for rain and says, 'Whatever Allah decrees is best.' His attitude combines effort with belief in
questions.A: the earlier scriptures
questions.B: the angels
questions.C: Qadar (divine decree)
questions.explanation: Belief in qadar does not remove the duty to take means; 'tie your camel and trust in Allah'.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: A student who fails an examination because he did not study says, 'It was destined; there was nothing I could do.' This is a misuse of the belief in qadar because
questions.A: examinations are not part of Allah's knowledge
questions.B: qadar applies only to prophets
questions.C: qadar concerns wealth and not education
questions.D: man is responsible for his choices and will be judged on them
questions.explanation: Qadar means Allah knows and permits all things, but humans choose and are accountable; using destiny to excuse laziness is wrong.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The Zabur was revealed to
questions.A: Musa (Moses)
questions.B: Dawud (David)
questions.C: Isa (Jesus)
questions.explanation: Tawrat to Musa, Zabur to Dawud, Injil to Isa, Qur'an to Muhammad; Suhuf to Ibrahim.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: Muslims believe in the earlier scriptures but follow the Qur'an alone because
questions.A: the Qur'an was revealed to all the earlier prophets in exactly the same words
questions.B: the earlier books were never revealed by Allah to any prophet at any time in history
questions.C: the earlier books were altered and the Qur'an confirms, corrects and supersedes them
questions.D: the earlier books were written in Arabic and are therefore included in the Qur'an
questions.explanation: The Qur'an is the final, preserved revelation and the criterion (muhaymin) over previous books (5:48).

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: Belief in the Hereafter affects a Muslim businessman by
questions.A: excusing him from paying Zakat on the profits of his business
questions.B: encouraging him to hoard goods until prices rise in the market
questions.C: permitting him to charge interest on the loans he gives to customers
questions.D: restraining him from fraud since he will account for every gain
questions.explanation: Accountability on the Day of Judgement is a powerful check on dishonest conduct.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The angel who is assigned to take the souls of people at death is
questions.A: Ridwan
questions.B: Malak al-Mawt (Izra'il)
questions.C: Mika'il
questions.explanation: The Angel of Death takes souls; Ridwan keeps Paradise; Malik keeps Hell.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: In Islam, 'ibadah' (worship) is best defined as
questions.A: the rituals performed in the mosque on Fridays and on the days of Eid
questions.B: the five daily prayers performed in congregation in the mosque
questions.C: everything Allah loves and is pleased with, in words and deeds, open or secret
questions.D: the acts of charity given openly in public so that others may follow
questions.explanation: Ibadah covers ritual acts and all lawful activities done with sincere intention to please Allah.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: A Muslim who earns a lawful living to feed his family with the intention of obeying Allah is
questions.A: excused from prayer while at work
questions.B: wasting time that should be spent in the mosque
questions.C: committing a sin by loving the world
questions.D: engaged in worship, because lawful work with good intention is ibadah
questions.explanation: The concept of worship in Islam is comprehensive; the Prophet said earning for one's family is charity.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: Acts of worship are classified by the law into five categories. An act whose performance is rewarded and whose omission is punished is
questions.A: mustahabb (mandub)
questions.B: fard (wajib)
questions.C: mubah
questions.explanation: Fard is obligatory; mustahabb is recommended; mubah is permissible; makruh is disliked; haram is forbidden.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The Jumu'ah prayer is fard 'ayn while the Janazah prayer is fard kifayah. The difference is that fard kifayah
questions.A: is only recommended and never obligatory
questions.B: must be performed by every individual Muslim
questions.C: is discharged for the whole community if some Muslims perform it
questions.explanation: Individual obligations (fard 'ayn) bind everyone; communal obligations (fard kifayah) bind the community until enough people fulfil them.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: Before every act of worship a Muslim must have niyyah (intention). The place of niyyah is
questions.A: the prayer mat
questions.B: the tongue
questions.C: the mosque
questions.explanation: Intention is a resolve of the heart; pronouncing it aloud is not required.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: Salah and Sawm are bodily acts of worship, Zakat is a financial act, while Hajj is
questions.A: purely financial
questions.B: both bodily and financial
questions.C: purely bodily
questions.explanation: Hajj requires physical effort and the means to travel, combining both categories.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: A Muslim who prays regularly but also cheats in trade has failed to understand that
questions.A: trade and business are outside the scope of religion altogether
questions.B: prayer is the only thing Allah requires from a Muslim in this life
questions.C: worship must transform character; prayer 'restrains from indecency and wrongdoing' (29:45)
questions.D: cheating is permitted for a person who prays regularly and fasts
questions.explanation: Ritual worship that does not improve conduct has missed its purpose.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: Which of the following is a condition of purity (taharah) required before Salah?
questions.A: reciting the whole Qur'an before the prayer
questions.B: wearing new clothes bought for prayer
questions.C: eating a full meal shortly before the prayer
questions.D: freedom from ritual impurity by wudu or ghusl
questions.explanation: Purity of body, clothes and place, and ritual purity through wudu or ghusl, are conditions of prayer.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: Ghusl (full bath) becomes obligatory for a Muslim after
questions.A: eating cooked food, drinking water or sleeping for more than an hour
questions.B: sexual intercourse, seminal discharge, menstruation or post-natal bleeding
questions.C: touching a dog, a cat or any other animal kept in the house
questions.D: sleeping in the afternoon, sneezing or laughing during the day
questions.explanation: Major ritual impurity (janabah, hayd, nifas) requires ghusl before prayer.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: Tayammum is performed by
questions.A: wiping over the socks with wet hands after washing the face
questions.B: washing the whole body with water from head to foot
questions.C: striking clean earth with the palms and wiping the face and hands
questions.D: rinsing the mouth and nose three times with clean water
questions.explanation: Tayammum (5:6) substitutes for wudu or ghusl when water is unavailable or harmful.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: Dhikr (remembrance of Allah) includes
questions.A: writing letters to relatives in other towns
questions.B: counting one's money at the end of the day
questions.C: listening to the news on the radio every evening
questions.D: saying Subhanallah, Alhamdulillah and Allahu Akbar
questions.explanation: Dhikr is glorifying, praising and magnifying Allah with the tongue and heart.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The Prophet (SAW) said, 'Du'a (supplication) is worship.' A Muslim who asks only Allah for his needs is
questions.A: neglecting the five pillars
questions.B: practising a central act of ibadah
questions.C: doing something optional with no reward
questions.explanation: Supplication expresses dependence on Allah and is itself worship.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: Bid'ah in worship refers to
questions.A: reading the Qur'an in a newly built mosque before it has been officially opened
questions.B: performing the sunnah prayers regularly before and after the obligatory ones
questions.C: introducing into religion practices that have no basis in the Qur'an or Sunnah
questions.D: using a microphone and loudspeakers for the adhan and the Friday sermon
questions.explanation: The Prophet said whoever introduces into this religion what is not of it, it is rejected; worldly tools are not bid'ah.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The pillars of Islam are five while the articles of faith are six. The pillar that is a declaration made with the tongue is
questions.A: Hajj
questions.B: Salah
questions.C: Zakat
questions.explanation: The Shahadah is the testimony of faith; the other pillars are acts of the body and wealth.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The five daily prayers were made obligatory on the Muslims during
questions.A: the battle of Badr
questions.B: the Isra' and Mi'raj
questions.C: the Farewell Pilgrimage
questions.explanation: On the Mi'raj the prayers were prescribed, reduced from fifty to five with the reward of fifty.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The number of rak'ahs in the fard of Maghrib prayer is
questions.A: four
questions.B: two
questions.C: three
questions.explanation: Fajr 2, Zuhr 4, Asr 4, Maghrib 3, Isha 4.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: A Muslim wakes up after sunrise having missed Fajr. He should
questions.A: give sadaqah in place of the prayer
questions.B: wait until the next Fajr and pray twice
questions.C: fast that day instead of praying
questions.D: perform the missed prayer (qada') as soon as he remembers
questions.explanation: The Prophet said whoever forgets a prayer or sleeps through it should pray it when he remembers.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: Which of the following is a pillar (rukn) of Salah, without which the prayer is invalid?
questions.A: saying the opening supplication (du'a al-istiftah)
questions.B: recitation of Surah Al-Fatihah in every rak'ah
questions.C: raising the hands at takbir
questions.explanation: The Prophet said there is no prayer for one who does not recite the Opening of the Book; the others are sunnah.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: A Muslim who forgets the number of rak'ahs he has prayed and adds an extra one should, before the salam,
questions.A: make tayammum and continue
questions.B: repeat the whole prayer from the beginning
questions.C: perform two prostrations of forgetfulness (sujud as-sahw)
questions.D: leave the prayer and pray later
questions.explanation: Sujud as-sahw compensates for additions, omissions or doubts in the prayer.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: Which of the following invalidates Salah?
questions.A: praying on a mat spread on the ground
questions.B: closing the eyes briefly in prostration
questions.C: reciting a long surah after Al-Fatihah
questions.explanation: Deliberate speech, eating, laughing aloud, turning from the qiblah and breaking wudu nullify the prayer.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The Janazah (funeral) prayer differs from other prayers in that it
questions.A: has ten rak'ahs
questions.B: has four takbirs and is performed standing without bowing or prostration
questions.C: is prayed only at night
questions.D: requires the worshipper to face away from the qiblah
questions.explanation: Salat al-Janazah consists of four takbirs with recitation, blessings on the Prophet and du'a for the deceased, all standing.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The two Eid prayers differ from the Friday prayer in that the Eid prayer
questions.A: has four rak'ahs and is prayed silently
questions.B: is performed at night after the Isha prayer
questions.C: has extra takbirs and its sermon comes after the prayer
questions.D: is obligatory only for women and children
questions.explanation: Eid prayer has additional takbirs in each rak'ah and the khutbah follows the prayer; on Friday the khutbah precedes it.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The Witr prayer is performed
questions.A: only in Ramadan, with twenty rak'ahs
questions.B: before Fajr, with four rak'ahs
questions.C: at noon on Friday, with two rak'ahs
questions.D: after Isha, with an odd number of rak'ahs
questions.explanation: Witr ('odd') closes the night prayers; the Prophet said 'make the last of your prayer at night Witr'.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The Tarawih prayer is offered
questions.A: at dawn on the morning of Eid day
questions.B: in congregation after Isha during Ramadan
questions.C: during an eclipse of the sun or the moon
questions.D: in times of drought to ask for rain
questions.explanation: Tarawih is the night prayer of Ramadan; Umar organised it in congregation behind one imam.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: A Muslim arriving late joins the congregation while the imam is in the second rak'ah of Zuhr. After the imam's salam he should
questions.A: repeat the whole prayer alone from the start
questions.B: make salam with the imam and leave
questions.C: stand up and complete the rak'ah he missed
questions.D: join another mosque for the same prayer
questions.explanation: The latecomer (masbuq) follows the imam and then makes up what he missed.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The qiblah was changed from Jerusalem to the Ka'bah in Makkah
questions.A: on the night of the Mi'raj
questions.B: during the boycott in Shi'b Abi Talib
questions.C: after the conquest of Makkah
questions.D: in the second year after the Hijrah, in Madinah
questions.explanation: Surah 2:144 commanded the change about sixteen months after the Hijrah; the mosque where it happened is Masjid al-Qiblatayn.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The conditions (shurut) of Salah include all of the following EXCEPT
questions.A: purity from ritual impurity
questions.B: reciting the Qur'an from a printed copy
questions.C: covering the awrah
questions.explanation: Purity, covering, facing the qiblah, the time having entered and intention are conditions; a printed Qur'an is not required.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The person chosen to lead the congregational prayer should preferably be the one who
questions.A: is the tallest man in the congregation
questions.B: is the wealthiest man in the congregation
questions.C: recites the Qur'an best and knows the Sunnah
questions.D: arrived last at the mosque for the prayer
questions.explanation: The Prophet said the people should be led by the one who recites the Book of Allah best.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: A traveller on a long journey combines Zuhr and Asr at the time of Zuhr. This concession is called
questions.A: i'tikaf
questions.B: qada' (making up prayers)
questions.C: sujud as-sahw
questions.explanation: Jam' at-taqdim (combining early) or jam' at-ta'khir (combining late) is allowed for travellers and in cases of need.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The sunnah mu'akkadah (emphasised sunnah) prayers before Fajr consist of
questions.A: four rak'ahs
questions.B: two rak'ahs
questions.C: three rak'ahs
questions.explanation: The two rak'ahs before Fajr are the most emphasised; the Prophet said they are better than the world and all it contains.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The Friday prayer is not obligatory on
questions.A: civil servants
questions.B: traders in the market
questions.C: women, travellers, the sick and children
questions.explanation: Jumu'ah is obligatory on free, adult, resident, healthy male Muslims; others may attend but are not bound.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: During the Friday sermon (khutbah), a Muslim in the mosque should
questions.A: read a newspaper
questions.B: chat quietly with his neighbour
questions.C: make up missed prayers
questions.explanation: The Prophet said whoever tells his companion 'be quiet' during the khutbah has spoken vainly; silence is required.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: A sick Muslim who cannot stand should pray
questions.A: by paying money to someone to pray for him
questions.B: sitting, and if unable, lying on his side, with gestures for bowing and prostration
questions.C: only after he recovers, making up all missed prayers at once
questions.explanation: The Prophet told Imran ibn Husayn: pray standing; if you cannot, sitting; if you cannot, on your side.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: Sujud (prostration) in Salah is performed on seven parts of the body: the forehead with the nose, the two hands, the two knees and
questions.A: the two shoulders
questions.B: the two elbows
questions.C: the toes of the two feet
questions.explanation: The Prophet said he was commanded to prostrate on seven bones.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The three times when voluntary prayers are disliked are
questions.A: during Ramadan, Shawwal and Dhul-Hijjah
questions.B: after Fajr, after Zuhr and after Maghrib
questions.C: on Friday, Saturday and Sunday
questions.D: at sunrise, when the sun is at its zenith, and at sunset
questions.explanation: The Prophet forbade praying at the moments of sunrise, zenith and sunset.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The Salat al-Istikharah is prayed by a Muslim who
questions.A: wants rain to fall during a long drought
questions.B: seeks Allah's guidance before making an important decision
questions.C: witnesses an eclipse of the sun or the moon
questions.D: is about to set out on a long journey by air
questions.explanation: Istikharah is two rak'ahs followed by a special supplication asking Allah to choose what is best.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The prayer performed during a drought to ask Allah for rain is
questions.A: Salat ad-Duha
questions.B: Salat al-Kusuf
questions.C: Salat al-Istisqa'
questions.explanation: Istisqa' is the rain prayer; Kusuf is the eclipse prayer; Khawf is the prayer in fear of an enemy.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The purpose of Salah is described in the Qur'an as
questions.A: replacing the need for honesty and fair dealing in the worshipper's trade
questions.B: increasing the wealth of the worshipper and protecting his business from loss
questions.C: making the worshipper famous and respected in the community where he lives
questions.D: restraining the worshipper from shameful and evil deeds and remembering Allah
questions.explanation: Surah Al-Ankabut 29:45: 'Prayer restrains from indecency and wrongdoing, and the remembrance of Allah is greater.'

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The adhan is called before the prayer while the iqamah is called
questions.A: after the prayer has ended
questions.B: immediately before the congregation begins the prayer
questions.C: only on Fridays and on the two days of Eid
questions.explanation: The iqamah signals the actual start of the congregational prayer.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: Zakat is obligatory on wealth that has reached the nisab and has been held for
questions.A: six months
questions.B: one month
questions.C: one full lunar year (hawl)
questions.explanation: The conditions of Zakat on money and trade goods are ownership, nisab and the passage of a lunar year.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The rate of Zakat on cash, gold, silver and trade goods is
questions.A: 20 per cent
questions.B: 10 per cent
questions.C: 5 per cent
questions.explanation: One-fortieth (2.5%) is due on monetary wealth above the nisab after a year.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: A farmer irrigates his rice field with a petrol pump. The Zakat due on his harvest is
questions.A: 10 per cent (ushr)
questions.B: 5 per cent (half ushr)
questions.C: 2.5 per cent
questions.explanation: Crops watered by rain or rivers pay 10%; crops irrigated at cost pay 5%.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: Mallam Bello has 60 sheep that graze freely for the whole year. The Zakat due on them is
questions.A: three sheep
questions.B: two sheep
questions.C: one sheep
questions.explanation: From 40 to 120 sheep, one sheep is due.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: A trader has stock worth ₦2,000,000, cash of ₦500,000 and debts owed to suppliers of ₦500,000. The Zakat due on his trade is

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: Zakat al-Fitr must be paid
questions.A: after the Eid prayer
questions.B: before the Eid al-Fitr prayer
questions.C: on the first day of Ramadan
questions.explanation: Paid after the Eid prayer it counts only as ordinary sadaqah.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: Which of the following persons may NOT receive Zakat from Alhaji Sule?
questions.A: a debtor who cannot pay
questions.B: a poor neighbour
questions.C: his own poor son
questions.explanation: Zakat cannot be given to those one is obliged to maintain (parents, children, wife).

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: Zakat collectors (al-amilin alayha) are entitled to a share of Zakat because
questions.A: they have memorised the whole Qur'an and teach it to others
questions.B: they are always poor and have no other source of income
questions.C: they are relatives of the caliph or the ruler of the state
questions.D: they work to collect and distribute it, as stated in Qur'an 9:60
questions.explanation: The Qur'an lists those employed to administer Zakat among its eight recipients.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The category 'al-mu'allafat qulubuhum' among the recipients of Zakat refers to
questions.A: the memorisers of the whole Qur'an
questions.B: those whose hearts are to be reconciled to Islam
questions.C: the imams who lead the prayers in the mosques
questions.D: the soldiers who fight in the army
questions.explanation: New Muslims or those inclined to Islam may be given Zakat to strengthen their attachment.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The literal meaning of Zakat is
questions.A: pilgrimage and sacrifice
questions.B: fasting and patience
questions.C: purification and growth
questions.explanation: Zakat purifies the giver's wealth and soul and causes wealth to grow in blessing.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The first caliph, Abu Bakr, fought the tribes that refused to pay Zakat after the Prophet's death because
questions.A: the Prophet had ordered him before his death to conquer Persia and Byzantium
questions.B: he needed the money to build a palace for himself and the other companions
questions.C: the tribes had also refused to fast in Ramadan and to pray in congregation
questions.D: Zakat is an obligation equal in status to Salah and cannot be separated from it
questions.explanation: Abu Bakr said: 'By Allah, I will fight whoever separates prayer from Zakat.'

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: Which of the following is exempt from Zakat?
questions.A: gold jewellery kept as an investment
questions.B: a house in which the owner lives and the car he uses
questions.C: cash savings above the nisab kept for a year
questions.D: goods bought for resale in a shop
questions.explanation: Personal-use items (home, car, clothes, tools) are not zakatable.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The economic significance of Zakat is that it
questions.A: redistributes wealth from the rich to the poor and discourages hoarding
questions.B: increases the wealth of the rich and makes the poor depend on them
questions.C: replaces all other forms of taxation levied by the government
questions.D: prevents Muslims from engaging in trade and accumulating wealth
questions.explanation: Zakat circulates wealth and reduces the gap between rich and poor.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: Zakat al-Fitr is paid on behalf of
questions.A: every member of the household, including infants
questions.B: the adult men of the household only
questions.C: the head of the family and his wife only
questions.D: the poor members of the household only
questions.explanation: The head of the household pays for himself and all dependants.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: A man finds buried treasure (rikaz) from pre-Islamic times on his land. The portion due to the treasury is
questions.A: one-fifth (20 per cent)
questions.B: one-fortieth (2.5 per cent)
questions.C: one-tenth (10 per cent)
questions.explanation: The Prophet said: 'On rikaz is the fifth (khums).'

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: Hajiya Amina gives ₦5,000 to a beggar on her way to the market whenever she wishes, without calculating any rate or year. This gift is
questions.A: sadaqah, because it is voluntary with no fixed rate or recipients
questions.B: Zakat, because every gift to the poor is Zakat
questions.C: kaffarah, because it expiates a broken oath
questions.D: fidyah, because it replaces a missed fast
questions.explanation: Zakat is a fixed obligation with specified recipients; sadaqah is voluntary charity given freely.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: Fasting in Ramadan was made obligatory in
questions.A: the second year after the Hijrah
questions.B: the first year of prophethood
questions.C: the year of the conquest of Makkah
questions.D: the tenth year after the Hijrah
questions.explanation: Surah 2:183-185 prescribing the fast was revealed in Sha'ban 2 AH, the same year as the change of qiblah.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The fast of Ramadan begins each day at
questions.A: the true dawn (fajr) and ends at sunset
questions.B: sunrise and ends at noon
questions.C: midnight and ends at sunrise
questions.explanation: The Qur'an says eat and drink until the white thread of dawn is distinct from the black thread, then complete the fast till night.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The Prophet (SAW) said: 'Fast when you see it (the new moon) and break your fast when you see it; if it is obscured, then complete thirty days.' A Muslim who begins Ramadan on the basis of a calendar without sighting or completing Sha'ban is
questions.A: departing from the Prophet's method of determining the month
questions.B: following the Sunnah of the Prophet exactly as he taught it
questions.C: obliged to fast sixty consecutive days as an expiation for his act
questions.D: excused from fasting for that year and the year that follows
questions.explanation: The lunar month is established by sighting the new moon or completing thirty days.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: A woman begins menstruating at 3 pm during a Ramadan fast. Her fast for that day
questions.A: is broken, and she must make up the day after Ramadan
questions.B: remains valid until sunset if she does not eat
questions.C: is valid but she must pay fidyah to the poor for it
questions.D: is valid if she performs ghusl before sunset
questions.explanation: Menstruation invalidates the fast; the missed days are made up later (qada').

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: A traveller on a long journey in Ramadan chooses not to fast. He must
questions.A: make up the missed days after Ramadan
questions.B: pay a fine to the mosque
questions.C: fast twice the number of days missed
questions.D: do nothing, as travel cancels the obligation permanently
questions.explanation: The concession for travellers and the sick requires qada' of the days missed (2:184).

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The Prophet (SAW) recommended breaking the fast with
questions.A: fresh or dry dates, or water
questions.B: a large meal of meat
questions.C: cold soft drinks
questions.explanation: He broke his fast with ripe dates, or dry dates, or a few sips of water before praying Maghrib.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The Prophet (SAW) said: 'Whoever does not give up false speech and acting on it, Allah has no need of his giving up food and drink.' This teaches that
questions.A: fasting must include abstaining from lying, backbiting and bad conduct
questions.B: eating during the day is permitted for those who do not tell lies
questions.C: fasting is only about hunger and thirst and nothing else matters
questions.D: a fasting person may tell small lies provided he does not eat
questions.explanation: The moral dimension of the fast is essential; abstaining from food alone does not achieve taqwa.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: Which of the following does NOT invalidate the fast?
questions.A: using a miswak or brushing the teeth
questions.B: eating food deliberately
questions.C: drinking a glass of water
questions.explanation: Cleaning the teeth, bathing, tasting food without swallowing and unintentional acts do not break the fast.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The fast of the day of Ashura falls on
questions.A: the 10th of Muharram
questions.B: the 27th of Rajab
questions.C: the 9th of Dhul-Hijjah
questions.explanation: Ashura (10 Muharram) commemorates Musa's deliverance; the Prophet fasted it and recommended fasting the 9th as well.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: Fasting is forbidden (haram) on
questions.A: the two Eid days and the days of Tashriq (11-13 Dhul-Hijjah)
questions.B: Mondays and Thursdays
questions.C: the white days (13th-15th of each month)
questions.explanation: The Prophet forbade fasting on the days of Eid and the days of eating and drinking at Mina.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: A Muslim fasts the six days of Shawwal after Ramadan. According to the Hadith, his reward is
questions.A: like fasting the whole year
questions.B: forgiveness of the sins of ten years
questions.C: a house in Paradise
questions.explanation: Ramadan is like ten months and six days like two months, making a year's fast.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: I'tikaf is
questions.A: secluding oneself in the mosque for worship, especially in the last ten days of Ramadan
questions.B: the pre-dawn meal taken before the fast begins, recommended by the Prophet
questions.C: the sacrifice offered on the morning of Eid al-Adha after the prayer
questions.D: the prayer performed in congregation after Isha in the nights of Ramadan
questions.explanation: The Prophet observed i'tikaf in the last ten nights of Ramadan seeking Laylat al-Qadr.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: According to the Qur'an, the purpose of fasting is that believers may
questions.A: attain taqwa (God-consciousness)
questions.B: lose weight and stay healthy
questions.C: save money spent on food
