questions.explanation: Surah 2:183 ends 'so that you may become righteous (la'allakum tattaqun)'.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The Prophet (SAW) said, 'Fasting is a shield.' A fasting person who is insulted should say
questions.A: 'I am fasting' and refrain from retaliating
questions.B: an insult twice as strong in reply
questions.C: nothing, but break his fast immediately
questions.D: a curse on the offender and his family
questions.explanation: The Hadith instructs the fasting person to say 'I am fasting' and avoid quarrels.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: A very sick person whose doctor says fasting will worsen his illness, but who is expected to recover, should
questions.A: not fast and make up the days later
questions.B: fast anyway to earn more reward
questions.C: pay fidyah and never make up
questions.explanation: Temporary illness permits breaking the fast with qada' later; permanent inability requires fidyah.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: Social benefits of fasting include
questions.A: sympathy for the hungry and generosity to the poor
questions.B: increased profits for food sellers
questions.C: reduced attendance at the mosque
questions.explanation: Experiencing hunger teaches empathy; Ramadan is a month of increased charity.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: Laylat al-Qadr should be sought, according to the Prophet (SAW), in
questions.A: the odd nights of the last ten nights of Ramadan
questions.B: the first night of Ramadan
questions.C: the night of the 15th of Sha'ban
questions.explanation: The Prophet said: 'Seek Laylat al-Qadr in the odd nights of the last ten of Ramadan.'

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The month in which the Qur'an was first revealed and in which Muslims fast is
questions.A: Ramadan
questions.B: Muharram
questions.C: Rajab
questions.explanation: Surah 2:185: 'The month of Ramadan in which the Qur'an was revealed.'

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The pilgrimage to Makkah is obligatory once in a lifetime on every Muslim who is
questions.A: adult, sane, free and able (physically and financially)
questions.B: over sixty years old and retired from work
questions.C: married with children of his own
questions.D: an Arab by birth and a resident of Makkah
questions.explanation: Qur'an 3:97: 'Pilgrimage to the House is a duty owed to Allah by people who are able to make the journey.'

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The Hajj rites take place mainly between the 8th and the 13th of the month of
questions.A: Dhul-Hijjah
questions.B: Ramadan
questions.C: Muharram
questions.explanation: The days of Hajj are 8 (Tarwiyah), 9 (Arafah), 10 (Nahr) and 11-13 (Tashriq) Dhul-Hijjah.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: A pilgrim performs Umrah first, comes out of ihram, and then enters ihram again for Hajj on the 8th of Dhul-Hijjah, offering a sacrifice. This type of Hajj is
questions.A: Tamattu'
questions.B: Ifrad
questions.C: Qiran
questions.explanation: Tamattu' separates Umrah and Hajj with a break; Qiran combines them in one ihram; Ifrad is Hajj alone.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: A Nigerian pilgrim flying to Jeddah must enter ihram before passing the miqat. The miqat stations were fixed by
questions.A: the Prophet (SAW) for pilgrims coming from different directions
questions.B: the Saudi government in 1950 to control the flow of pilgrims
questions.C: Caliph Umar after he had conquered Persia and Syria
questions.D: the tribe of Quraysh before the coming of Islam
questions.explanation: The Prophet designated Dhul-Hulayfah, Juhfah, Qarn al-Manazil, Yalamlam (and Dhat Irq) as miqats.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: While in ihram a male pilgrim may NOT
questions.A: wear sewn clothes, cover his head, use perfume or cut his hair
questions.B: drink water, eat cooked food or sleep at night in a tent
questions.C: speak to other pilgrims or greet them with the salam
questions.D: perform the five daily prayers or recite the Qur'an aloud
questions.explanation: The prohibitions of ihram include sewn garments and head covering for men, perfume, cutting hair or nails, hunting and marital relations.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The words recited repeatedly by pilgrims from the time they enter ihram, 'Labbayk Allahumma labbayk', are called
questions.A: the Talbiyah
questions.B: the Tashahhud
questions.C: the Takbir
questions.explanation: The Talbiyah declares 'Here I am, O Allah, here I am; You have no partner.'

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: On the 8th of Dhul-Hijjah (Yawm at-Tarwiyah) pilgrims
questions.A: proceed to Mina and spend the night there
questions.B: stand on the plain of Arafat
questions.C: stone the three pillars
questions.explanation: The pilgrims move to Mina on the 8th and go to Arafat on the morning of the 9th.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: After sunset on the Day of Arafah, pilgrims move to Muzdalifah, where they
questions.A: pray Maghrib and Isha together and collect pebbles for the stoning
questions.B: sacrifice their animals and distribute the meat to the poor
questions.C: perform the sa'y between the hills of Safa and Marwah
questions.D: shave their heads and put on their ordinary clothes
questions.explanation: At Muzdalifah pilgrims combine the two prayers, spend the night and gather pebbles.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: On the 10th of Dhul-Hijjah (Yawm an-Nahr) the pilgrim stones Jamrat al-Aqabah, offers his sacrifice, shaves or trims his hair and then performs
questions.A: Tawaf al-Ifadah, a pillar of Hajj
questions.B: Tawaf al-Qudum
questions.C: Tawaf al-Wada'
questions.explanation: Tawaf al-Ifadah (az-Ziyarah) on the day of sacrifice is one of the pillars of Hajj.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: Tawaf consists of going round the Ka'bah
questions.A: seven times anticlockwise, starting from the Black Stone
questions.B: three times clockwise, starting from Maqam Ibrahim
questions.C: seven times between Safa and Marwah
questions.explanation: Tawaf is seven circuits with the Ka'bah on the left, beginning and ending at the Black Stone.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The last rite a pilgrim performs before leaving Makkah is
questions.A: Tawaf al-Wada' (the farewell tawaf)
questions.B: the standing on the plain of Arafat
questions.C: the stoning of the pillars at Mina
questions.D: the sacrifice of a ram at Mina
questions.explanation: The Prophet ordered that no one should leave until his last act is at the House.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The pillars (arkan) of Hajj, without which the Hajj is invalid, include
questions.A: ihram, standing at Arafat, Tawaf al-Ifadah and sa'y
questions.B: stoning the jamarat and spending the night at Mina
questions.C: the farewell tawaf and drinking Zamzam
questions.D: praying at Maqam Ibrahim and kissing the Black Stone
questions.explanation: The arkan are ihram (intention), wuquf at Arafat, tawaf al-ifadah and sa'y; other acts are obligations (wajibat) or sunnah.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: A pilgrim who omits an obligatory act (wajib) of Hajj, such as spending the night at Muzdalifah, must
questions.A: offer a sacrifice (dam) as compensation
questions.B: repeat the whole Hajj the following year
questions.C: fast for sixty days
questions.explanation: Omitting a wajib is compensated by a sacrifice; omitting a rukn invalidates the Hajj.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The Ka'bah was built (or rebuilt) as a house of worship by
questions.A: Ibrahim and his son Isma'il
questions.B: Musa and Harun
questions.C: Dawud and Sulayman
questions.explanation: Surah 2:127: 'And when Ibrahim was raising the foundations of the House with Isma'il.'

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The well of Zamzam is associated with
questions.A: Hajar and her infant son Isma'il when she searched for water
questions.B: the digging of the trench around Madinah before the siege
questions.C: the Prophet's journey to Ta'if and his rejection there
questions.D: the battle of Badr and the wells seized by the Muslims
questions.explanation: Zamzam sprang up for Isma'il after Hajar ran between Safa and Marwah seeking water.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The Prophet (SAW) said: 'Whoever performs Hajj and does not commit obscenity or transgression returns as on the day his mother bore him.' This teaches that an accepted Hajj
questions.A: wipes out previous sins
questions.B: makes further prayer unnecessary
questions.C: guarantees wealth on return
questions.explanation: Hajj Mabrur has no reward but Paradise and cleanses the pilgrim of past sins.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: Social significance of Hajj is best seen in the fact that
questions.A: pilgrims of all races and classes wear the same simple dress and perform the same rites together
questions.B: only wealthy pilgrims are allowed to stand on the plain of Arafat on the ninth day
questions.C: each country performs its rites separately in its own camp at Mina and Arafat
questions.D: pilgrims trade goods with one another at Mina during the three days of Tashriq
questions.explanation: Hajj demonstrates the equality and unity of the ummah before Allah.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The Prophet (SAW) performed how many Hajj after the Hijrah?
questions.A: one, in 10 AH
questions.B: five, one each year
questions.C: three, in 8, 9 and 10 AH
questions.explanation: He performed only one Hajj, in 10 AH, and delivered the Farewell Sermon at Arafat.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: In Nigeria, the body responsible for organising and regulating the pilgrimage is
questions.A: the National Hajj Commission of Nigeria
questions.B: the Central Bank of Nigeria
questions.C: the Nigerian Ports Authority
questions.explanation: NAHCON, established in 2006, coordinates Hajj and Umrah operations with state pilgrims' welfare boards.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The literal meaning of the word 'jihad' is
questions.A: striving or exerting effort
questions.B: holy war
questions.C: pilgrimage
questions.explanation: Jihad means struggle in the cause of Allah, which takes many forms.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: A Muslim who spends his money to build a school for poor children, and a scholar who writes books defending Islam, are engaged respectively in
questions.A: jihad with wealth and jihad with the pen (knowledge)
questions.B: jihad by the sword and jihad by fasting
questions.C: greater and lesser pilgrimage
questions.explanation: Jihad bil-mal (wealth) and jihad bil-qalam (pen) are recognised forms of striving in Allah's cause.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The Qur'an says: 'Fight in the way of Allah those who fight you, but do not transgress; indeed Allah does not love transgressors' (2:190). This verse teaches that armed jihad
questions.A: is defensive and bound by limits
questions.B: may be waged against anyone at any time
questions.C: requires the killing of all prisoners
questions.D: is one of the five pillars
questions.explanation: Fighting is permitted against aggressors within strict ethical limits.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: Abu Bakr instructed his army: 'Do not kill women, children or the aged; do not cut down fruit trees; do not harm monks in their monasteries.' These instructions show that in Islam war
questions.A: must spare non-combatants and avoid needless destruction
questions.B: has no rules
questions.C: is aimed at converting people by force
questions.explanation: Islamic law of war protects civilians, property, crops and religious persons.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: A group kills innocent worshippers and market women and calls its actions jihad. According to the Qur'an (5:32), killing one innocent person is
questions.A: like killing all mankind, so such actions are not jihad but grave crimes
questions.B: a lesser form of jihad that is rewarded in the Hereafter
questions.C: permitted if the victims are not Muslims or are from another tribe
questions.D: acceptable if a leader of the group commands it in the name of religion
questions.explanation: Terrorism against innocents violates the clear text of the Qur'an and the practice of the Prophet.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: Self-discipline in Islam is developed most directly through
questions.A: fasting, which trains a Muslim to control hunger, thirst and desire
questions.B: accumulating wealth and property for the family
questions.C: avoiding all social contact with other people
questions.D: sleeping during the day and staying awake at night
questions.explanation: Sawm is a school of self-restraint and taqwa.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: A young man is tempted to join his friends in drinking and gambling but resists and goes to the mosque instead. He is engaged in
questions.A: jihad an-nafs (struggle against the lower self)
questions.B: jihad by the sword against the enemy
questions.C: Hajj at-Tamattu' during the month of Dhul-Hijjah
questions.D: sadaqah jariyah for the benefit of the poor
questions.explanation: Overcoming one's own desires and temptations is the inner struggle.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The Prophet (SAW) said: 'The mujahid is the one who strives against his own soul in obedience to Allah.' This Hadith emphasises
questions.A: the primacy of inner struggle over outward conflict
questions.B: that fighting is the only form of jihad
questions.C: that soldiers do not need discipline in battle
questions.D: that jihad is limited to the Arabs alone
questions.explanation: The Hadith redirects the concept of jihad to self-purification.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: Which of the following is a condition for legitimate armed jihad in Islamic law?
questions.A: it must be declared by a legitimate Muslim authority, not by private individuals or groups
questions.B: it may be declared by any Muslim who feels that he or his tribe has been offended
questions.C: it requires no warning to the enemy and no invitation to peace before fighting
questions.D: it must target the civilians of the enemy in order to be effective and quick
questions.explanation: Qital is the prerogative of the lawful ruler and is preceded by invitation to peace or treaty.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: Sabr (patience), an important element of self-discipline, includes
questions.A: patience in obedience, patience in avoiding sin and patience in adversity
questions.B: waiting for other people to do one's work while remaining idle
questions.C: keeping silent when one sees injustice being done to other people
questions.D: refusing to seek medical treatment when one is seriously ill
questions.explanation: Scholars identify three kinds of sabr: in worship, against sin and under trials.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: A student disciplines himself to wake for Fajr daily, study regularly and avoid time-wasting. His conduct reflects the Islamic value of
questions.A: mujahadah (striving to master oneself)
questions.B: israf (wasteful extravagance)
questions.C: ghaflah (heedless negligence)
questions.explanation: Mujahadah is the sustained effort to bring the self under the control of faith.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The Prophet (SAW) said, 'Wondrous is the affair of the believer: if good befalls him he is grateful, and if harm befalls him he is patient.' The disciplined believer therefore responds to every situation with
questions.A: gratitude or patience
questions.B: anger or despair
questions.C: boasting or complaint
questions.explanation: Shukr in ease and sabr in hardship make every condition good for the believer.
